newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet except for lone TSR20 deal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet except for lone TSR20 deal.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Wednesday except for a small transaction for TSR20 rubber, dealers said.
"The only thing done was for a forward shipment of TSR20 rubber. I heard there were also supposed to be some small deals for RSS3 rubber, but I don't know if it's been concluded," a dealer said.

Traders said sellers were again flocking into the market, but buyers remained scarce. Prices were also seen at lower levels in the local market due to tumbling prices in Japan where the key November contract shed 2.6 yen to 133.1.
"Prices are coming in at lower levels because prices in Japan really fell sharply this morning," a trader for a foreign rubber dealing house said.
"It's largely quiet although the level of activity this morning seem to be higher," a dealer said. "We may see a bit of active shortcovering later in the day."

At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 112.00-114.00 U.S. cents a kg from 114.50 cents. July RSS1 was indicated at 160.00-162.00 Singapore cents (US$1.12-$1.14) a kg from 162.00 cents. July TSR20 was indicated at 148.00 Singapore cents (US$1.04) a kg from 148.50 cents.
